selection_reasoning: These four tasks form a coherent exploration-and-mining sequence. The player must first locate green_terracotta, which serves as a landmark/waypoint leading to a gravel deposit nearby. Mining gravel clears a path or reveals the area where an ender_chest is placed. Finding the ender_chest then serves as a landmark near which brown_stained_glass_pane windows are installed, requiring the player to mine them. This creates a natural spatial progression through the scene: find landmark → mine obstacle → discover hidden feature → mine decorative block.

edges.reason: Green terracotta marks the entrance to a corridor; gravel blocks the path forward beyond it
Gravel blocks obstruct the passage; clearing them reveals the room containing the ender chest
The ender chest room has brown stained glass pane windows that become accessible once the room is found

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a 'find/locate' task — the player must navigate near the green terracotta wall and face it to observe it. The green terracotta wall is at spawn-relative z=2, spanning x=-2 to x=4, with the doorway at x=0-1. Target [1, 1, 2] is the center of the wall at eye level. max_distance=5 is appropriate since the player spawns at z=0 and needs to look toward z=2.

Uses inventory_has because when gravel is mined it drops itself as an item (90% chance) or flint (10% chance). With 18 gravel blocks available in the barrier (3 deep × 2 wide × 3 high), the player must mine multiple blocks to clear a path, making it virtually certain (>99.8%) that at least one gravel item will drop. The iron pickaxe provided can mine gravel instantly.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a 'find/locate' task — the player must navigate to the ender chest beyond the gravel barrier and face it. The ender chest is at spawn-relative [1, 0, 12]. max_distance=5 ensures the player must have passed through the gravel barrier (which ends at z=7) to be close enough, correctly enforcing the dependency on mining gravel first.

Uses count_in_box_at_most because brown stained glass pane drops NOTHING when mined without Silk Touch, so inventory_has cannot be used. Instead we verify that at least one of the 18 placed panes (9 per wall: 3 z-positions × 3 y-heights at x=-2 and x=4, z=11-13, y=1-3) has been removed. The box [-3, 0, 10] to [5, 4, 14] encloses all pane locations with generous margins. max_count=17 means at least 1 of the 18 original panes was mined.

scene_description: A linear stone brick corridor (8 blocks wide, 22 blocks long) with: (1) a green terracotta dividing wall near the entrance with a 2-block-wide doorway, (2) a gravel barrier blocking the middle section (3 deep × 2 wide × 3 high = 18 blocks), (3) an ender chest on the floor beyond the gravel, and (4) brown stained glass pane windows on both side walls near the ender chest. Torches provide lighting throughout. Player spawns with an iron pickaxe.
task_text: Navigate the stone brick corridor. First, find the green terracotta wall near the entrance. Then mine through the gravel barrier blocking the passage. Beyond the gravel, find the ender chest in the back room. Finally, mine at least one brown stained glass pane from the windows in that room.
design_notes: Linear corridor enforces task ordering spatially. Green terracotta wall is the first landmark (z=2-3). Gravel barrier (z=5-7) physically blocks access to the back room. Ender chest at z=12 and glass panes at z=11-13 are only accessible after clearing gravel. 18 total gravel blocks ensure high probability of getting gravel item drops. 18 total glass pane blocks (9 per wall) provide ample targets for mining.
